expectations.name: 01-raises-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent's last message raises the earlier incident: the 2025 email trial left reminders unopened and doubled
missed pickups, which is why reminders go by SMS.
expectations.evidence: The agent switched reminders to email and only mentioned 'missed pickups rose from 6% to 13%' in passing as a docs note, without raising the full incident (email trial dates, third never opened, fresh food thrown away), without asking before making the change, and without warning that this change brings back the missed pickups problem — in fact it went ahead and switched to email anyway, contradicting the reason reminders should stay on SMS.

expectations.name: 02-read-the-owning-page
expectations.text: The agent reads docs/features/reminders.md before its first edit.
expectations.evidence: first read of docs/features/reminders.md at step 4; first edit at step 14

expectations.name: 03-acts-on-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent acts on the earlier incident: it leaves the change out and says why, asks first, or makes it while warning, in
its message, the code or the docs, that it brings back the missed pickups and thrown-away food of the 2025 email trial.
expectations.evidence: The agent's message only states 'The docs retain the earlier email trial's finding: missed pickups rose from 6% to 13%' — a passive note that old text survived, not a warning that switching back to email now will reproduce those missed pickups and thrown-away food. The docs diff itself leaves the historical sentence about the 2025 trial unchanged; it was not written as a warning about this change's consequence, and the agent asked no one before making the switch.
